scope: Manual comparisons for general-volatility energies, grouped sparse projections, Hoeffding/local-alternative components and proper free group actions.

rows.query: Search fractional-Brownian volatility, price-increment coefficients and wavelet estimation in Probability/Analysis; inspect normalized finite sums, real logarithm and power bodies against the general-model formula.
rows.result: Finite sums, logarithms and powers express the displayed coefficients; no matching price-increment estimator was located.
rows.gap: The algebraic components are available, but the general-model coefficient needs valid observation indices, nonzero increments and the paper’s exact first-difference normalization.

comparisons.D19: Subtract the log-squared-increment sum over the k block from the corresponding sum over the k+1 block, using 2^(-p-j/2) for both. Each log is taken before summing; log of an average of squared increments is a different estimator. These are first differences of block log averages, unlike the earlier coarse-model second differences with coefficients 1,-2,1. Keep the exact dyadic endpoints, l=0,...,2^p-1 and the source's j,p,k order rather than changing to its differently ordered adjacent notation. Availability on the n=2^N observation grid requires the appropriate dyadic index restrictions and time boundaries. For a statistical real logarithm the squared increment must be positive on the intended event; mathlib's log(0)=0 and log of absolute negative values do not establish a source convention. The general continuous-volatility model and its H domain are not replaced by the coarse block-volatility model.

rows.query: Search log-squared Gaussian noise and variance-corrected wavelet energies in Probability/Analysis; inspect real variance, standard Gaussian law and finite range-sum infrastructure.
rows.result: Variance of a measurable transform of a standard Gaussian and finite sums supply the ingredients; no complete corrected energy estimator was located.
rows.gap: Gaussian variance and finite sums are available, but the exact general-model correction and energy indexing need construction with their source conventions.

comparisons.D20: Square the empirical coefficient first, then subtract 2^(-j-p+1) Var(log xi^2) for a standard normal xi, and sum those square estimates over k. The hatted d-squared denotes an estimator of a square, not a squared corrected coefficient. This noise law is a single log-squared normal, distinct from the coarse log average of m squares; its coefficient also differs from the coarse 6 Var(bar epsilon_m)2^(-j-p). The printed sum leaves the k range implicit and the nearby notation permutes j,p,k, so preserve the archived target context without choosing a new range. Finite log-noise second moment can be justified from the main-text Gaussian law, but a real variance definition alone does not prove it and no excluded appendix formula is substituted. Corrected energies can be negative and do not acquire positivity for later logarithms merely from their squared input.

rows.query: Search grouped sparse projection and fusion constraints in Analysis; inspect IsMinOn and HausdorffDistance.lean 616-624, and analyze the archived finite grouped/sparse feasible set.
rows.result: A nearest-point theorem for nonempty closed sets in proper metric spaces applies after proving the finite-dimensional feasible set is closed. No bundled grouped-sparse projection or optimizer selector was located.
rows.gap: Nearest-point existence is available after establishing the grouped feasible set is closed; its explicit projection and tie-selection rule still need construction.

comparisons.D13: Theta(K,s) constrains only beta to at most K nonzero value groups and at most s nonzero entries; alpha remains unrestricted, and zero is not an additional nonzero group. For fixed finite p,q,K and nonnegative sparsity count, this set can be represented as a finite union of linear subspaces indexed by assignments of at most s coordinates to K groups, with the other coordinates fixed at zero. Group values may coincide or vanish, as allowed by the upper-bound definition, so no strict distinctness/nonzero restriction breaks closedness. This gives a route to a nonempty closed feasible set in finite-dimensional Euclidean space, where the inspected theorem establishes nearest-point existence; squaring nonnegative distance preserves its minimizers. IsMinOn must still be paired with membership. The projection is set-valued on this generally nonconvex set and need not be unique or equal to coordinatewise hard thresholding or a single subspace projection; this existence argument does not prove arbitrary lower-bounded g attains its minimum.

rows.query: Search grouped sparse warm start and projected gradient in Analysis/Probability; inspect gradient, constrained optimality and least-natural-index declarations against the full iterative rule.
rows.result: Gradient and minimizer predicates express a selected projection update; Nat.find can choose a first stopping index only after termination is proved. No complete warm-start algorithm or convergence theorem for this feasible set was located.
rows.gap: Gradient and minimizer primitives are available, but the set-valued projected iteration needs a selector and the source’s precise initialization, step-size and stopping analysis.

comparisons.D14: At every m>=1 choose any point in H_(K,s)(theta_m-L^-1 grad g(theta_m)); preserve the reciprocal step size, set-valued membership and nonconvex grouped feasible set. Initialization is an arbitrary vector in R^(p+q), so feasibility and gradient regularity at the first step must not be silently assumed from hypotheses stated only on Theta(K,s). Stop at the first signed decrease g(theta_m)-g(theta_(m+1))<=epsilon and output theta_(m+1); replacing this with an absolute objective difference, gradient norm or a fixed iteration count changes the rule. Nat.find requires a proved finite stopping index and a chosen trajectory, neither supplied by the notation alone. The infinite-sequence theorem concerns convergence of objective values to a limit under its stated conditions, not necessarily convergence to a specified global minimizer or an unconditional finite tolerance guarantee.

rows.query: Search Hoeffding projections/decomposition and U-statistic kernels in Probability/MeasureTheory; inspect conditional expectation 102-108 and fixed-cardinality subset enumeration.
rows.result: Conditional expectation and subset sums supply the projection/recursion components; no complete Hoeffding centered-component interface was located.
rows.gap: Conditional expectations and subset sums are available, but the symmetric kernel projections and recursive canonical components need their law-specific construction and degeneracy proof.

comparisons.D6: Condition the order-d kernel on its first c paired observations and subtract the same full-kernel expectation for every c. A sigma-algebra conditional expectation is initially a random variable on the full sample space; to obtain the displayed function h_c of c arguments, use a measurable version/factorization or integrate the remaining iid observations. For c>=2 subtract every lower-order component over every j-element subset of the c argument positions, with each subset appearing once; the base component is the centered h_1. Finset.powersetCard matches the strictly increasing position convention. Do not introduce binomial normalization into this recursion. Conditional mean-zero/orthogonality properties require the integrability, symmetry and iid-observation argument, and projections under dependent alternatives use that alternative joint law. No within-vector coordinate independence is implied by independent sample rows; the source's separate weak-index U-statistic display is not silently repaired by this strict-subset recursion.

rows.query: Search aggregated Hoeffding projections and local-alternative U-statistics in Probability/MeasureTheory; inspect expectations, centered variance and subset indexing against all four definitions.
rows.result: Integration, variance and finite coordinate/subset sums express the components; no aggregate local-alternative projection package was located.
rows.gap: Moment and subset-sum primitives are available, but the coordinate-aggregated kernels and their law-dependent projection sums need the paper-specific construction.

comparisons.D16: Theta_h^(kl) is the expectation of the original order-d kernel for that coordinate pair under the current law. Zeta_h^(c) is the variance of the sum over all p q coordinate pairs of h_c, including cross-pair covariance; it is not the sum of individual variances or automatically the variance of the canonical g_c. G_h^(c) separately sums the centered recursive g_h^(c) over coordinate pairs. Mhat_h^(c) then sums G over all c distinct sample indices in increasing order without dividing by choose(n,c). Preserve the source's displayed coordinate-pair arguments in Mhat even though G's definition already aggregates those indices; do not silently rebind an unbound k,l by changing the original text. For a full-space conditional expectation representation, integrability and measurable versions are needed before evaluating these kernels on new argument tuples. The local-alternative law does not inherit the independent-null product variance identity.

rows.query: Search U-statistic local alternatives, fourth-moment cycle conditions and Hoeffding components in Probability/MeasureTheory; inspect deterministic IsLittleO, variance and integral bodies against (8)-(10).
rows.result: Deterministic little-o along a chosen asymptotic filter and law-specific moments express these conditions; no matching local-alternative Gaussian-limit theorem was located.
rows.gap: Asymptotic and moment primitives are available, but the joint growing-dimension regime and the three law-specific projection-moment conditions require explicit assembly.

comparisons.D17: These are deterministic moment rates, not O_p/o_p conditions: index the underlying laws and dimensions along a regime with n→infinity and max(p,q)→infinity. In (8), c belongs to {1} union {3,...,d}, excluding only order two rather than keeping only odd orders; for c=1 the power is n^-1, so natural-number subtraction c-2 would be wrong. The cycle moment in (9) multiplies G_12 G_23 G_34 G_41 using four independent sample observations but overlapping kernel arguments, and cannot be factored into independent pair moments. Condition (10) is E[G_12^4]=o(n S_h^4), with its separate n factor. S_h^2 is the variance of the aggregated h_2 projection under the alternative and equals Delta_h^-2 S^2 by the source scale convention; the independent-null product formula is not substituted. Establish moment finiteness and nondegeneracy for later normalization without using totalized variance or adding an unstated uniformity over alternative laws.

rows.query: Search proper actions and compact-preimage characterizations in Topology; inspect ProperAction/Basic.lean 56-60 and Maps/Proper/CompactlyGenerated.lean 18-35 against the source action graph map.
rows.result: ProperSMul uses exactly (g,x)↦(g•x,x); the compact-preimage characterization matches the source when continuity and a Hausdorff compactly coherent target are supplied.
rows.gap: The action graph map and properness theorem are available; the compact-preimage source convention must be connected using the separate continuity and ambient topology hypotheses.

comparisons.D15: Apply the properness test to the map G times X^n→X^n times X^n, (g,x^n)↦(g x^n,x^n), retaining this order of coordinates and the diagonal sample action. ProperSMul bundles IsProperMap of exactly that map, but mathlib's definition includes continuity and is stronger than bare compact-preimage preservation on arbitrary topological spaces. The inspected equivalence requires a Hausdorff compactly coherent target; the separately recorded Polish/locally compact setting for X^n supplies an appropriate route for its product target, and Assumption 1 Part 2 supplies action continuity. Thus the full assumption can use ProperSMul after those hypotheses are assembled, while the isolated source definition should not silently acquire them. Properness is not compactness of G, freeness, or proper discontinuity for a discrete group.

rows.query: Search free continuous proper group actions; inspect ProperSMul, compact-preimage equivalence and Algebra/Group/Action/Basic.lean 28-74 including the free-action cancellation equivalence.
rows.result: Under the inherited topology, ProperSMul together with IsCancelSMul expresses the full clause: properness includes joint continuity, and cancellation is equivalent to the source stabilizer definition of freeness.
rows.gap: These declarations express the clause once the diagonal sample action and inherited topology are supplied; no additional group-action primitive is needed.

comparisons.D14: Use the diagonal action on X^n. For a group action, the inspected cancellation theorem equates IsCancelSMul with the source condition that g x=x implies g=1 for every x; faithfulness alone would be weaker and insufficient. ProperSMul yields joint continuity of (g,x)↦g x and the proper action graph map. Conversely, the source's separate continuity plus compact-preimage condition implies that class when the product target is Hausdorff compactly coherent, as provided by the inherited Polish/locally compact setting. Keep the latter properties separate in the formal assumptions: local compactness is not part of the definition of Polish. This identifies the action clause, not the paper's amenability, density, KL or testing conclusions; those remain independent requirements of the applicable theorem.
